title: The Jerusalem Council, Paul and Barnabas Separate

questions.question: What did certain men from Judea teach that threatened to divide the church?
options: "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."
"Unless you keep all the Jewish feast days, you cannot be saved."
"Unless you eat only clean foods, you are not fully saved."
"Unless you learn Hebrew and read the Torah, you are not saved."
questions.correctAnswer: "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."
questions.explanation: Acts 15:1 (ESV): "But some men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers, 'Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.'"

questions.question: Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and debate with these men. Who did the church appoint to go up to Jerusalem to settle this?
options: Paul and Barnabas, with some others from their group
Silas and Judas Barsabbas as impartial mediators
The seven deacons as the church's representatives
Peter and John, who were already in Antioch
questions.correctAnswer: Paul and Barnabas, with some others from their group
questions.explanation: Acts 15:2 (ESV): "And after Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and debate with them, Paul and Barnabas and some of the others were appointed to go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and the elders about this question."

questions.question: At the Jerusalem council, some believers of the party of the Pharisees stood up and declared what was required for Gentile believers?
options: That they must be circumcised and ordered to keep the law of Moses
That they must be baptized by one of the twelve apostles directly
That they must observe the Sabbath and Jewish feast days fully
That they must study under a Jewish rabbi for one year first
questions.correctAnswer: That they must be circumcised and ordered to keep the law of Moses
questions.explanation: Acts 15:5 (ESV): "But some believers who belonged to the party of the Pharisees rose up and said, 'It is necessary to circumcise them and to order them to keep the law of Moses.'"

questions.question: Peter reminded the council that God had chosen him to preach to Gentiles and had given them the Holy Spirit just as to Jews, making no distinction. He said God cleansed their hearts "by..."?
options: faith
circumcision
water baptism
the Law
questions.explanation: Acts 15:9 (ESV): "and he made no distinction between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith."

questions.question: Peter rebuked the idea of requiring the Gentiles to keep the Law, saying: "Now, therefore, why are you putting God to the test by placing a yoke on the neck of the disciples that neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear? But we believe that we will be saved through the grace..."?
options: "of the Lord Jesus, just as they will."
"that God gives freely to all who repent."
"poured out on those who believe in his name."
"given through faith and not human effort."
questions.correctAnswer: "of the Lord Jesus, just as they will."
questions.explanation: Acts 15:11 (ESV): "But we believe that we will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will."

questions.question: James, who presided at the council, quoted from Amos to support accepting Gentiles. The portion of Amos agreed that God would rebuild the fallen dwelling (tent) of David so that the rest of mankind might seek the Lord, including "all the Gentiles who are called by..."?
options: my name
his grace
the covenant
his love
questions.explanation: Acts 15:17 (ESV): "...that the remnant of mankind may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who are called by my name, says the Lord..."

questions.question: What four requirements did the Jerusalem council require of Gentile believers?
options: Abstain from things polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from what has been strangled, and from blood
Circumcision, Sabbath observance, dietary laws, and holy day celebrations
Baptism, repentance, giving to the poor, and prayer
Learning Hebrew, studying Torah, attending synagogue, and tithing
questions.correctAnswer: Abstain from things polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from what has been strangled, and from blood
questions.explanation: Acts 15:20 (ESV): "...but should write to them to abstain from the things polluted by idols, and from sexual immorality, and from what has been strangled, and from blood."

questions.question: Who were appointed to carry the letter from the Jerusalem council to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas?
options: Judas called Barsabbas and Silas
John Mark and Barnabas's cousin
Timothy and Titus from among the Gentiles
Two of the original twelve apostles
questions.explanation: Acts 15:22 (ESV): "Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They sent Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers."

questions.question: The letter from the council began: "The apostles and the elders, your brothers, To the brothers who are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, greetings." What did it say about the troublemakers who had disturbed them?
options: They went out from the Jerusalem church without authorization
They were false apostles condemned by the Jerusalem elders
They were Pharisees who had not truly accepted Christ
They were expelled from the church for causing division
questions.correctAnswer: They went out from the Jerusalem church without authorization
questions.explanation: Acts 15:24 (ESV): "Since we have heard that some persons have gone out from us and troubled you with words, unsettling your minds, although we gave them no instructions,"

questions.question: What reason did Paul give for not wanting to take John Mark on the second missionary journey?
options: He had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work
He was too young and inexperienced for the hazardous journey ahead
He had spoken against Paul's authority before the Jerusalem council
He had refused to preach to Gentiles during the first journey
questions.correctAnswer: He had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work
questions.explanation: Acts 15:38 (ESV): "But Paul thought best not to take with them one who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work."

questions.question: The sharp disagreement over John Mark resulted in Paul and Barnabas separating. Who did each take as their new companion?
options: Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus; Paul chose Silas and went through Syria and Cilicia
Barnabas took Silas to Asia; Paul took Mark to Macedonia
Barnabas went back to Jerusalem; Paul took Timothy to Galatia
Barnabas and Mark went to Antioch; Paul and Silas returned to Lystra
questions.correctAnswer: Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus; Paul chose Silas and went through Syria and Cilicia
questions.explanation: Acts 15:39-41 (ESV): "And Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed away to Cyprus, but Paul chose Silas and departed, having been commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord. And he went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches."

questions.question: Who presided over the Jerusalem council and gave the final ruling?
options: James, the brother of Jesus
Peter the apostle
The high priest Caiaphas
The eleven remaining apostles jointly
questions.explanation: Acts 15:13,19 (ESV): "After they finished speaking, James replied... Therefore my judgment is..."

questions.question: How did the Antioch church respond when they heard the letter from Jerusalem read?
options: They rejoiced at its encouragement
They argued over its requirements
They sent it immediately to all the Gentile churches
They praised Paul and Barnabas for their work
questions.explanation: Acts 15:31 (ESV): "And when they had read it, they rejoiced because of its encouragement."

questions.question: Judas and Silas were described as prophets. What did they do for the brothers in Antioch?
options: Encouraged and strengthened them with many words
Delivered messages predicting future persecution
Performed signs and wonders among the believers
Settled disputes about the interpretation of the letter
questions.correctAnswer: Encouraged and strengthened them with many words
questions.explanation: Acts 15:32 (ESV): "And Judas and Silas, who were themselves prophets, encouraged and strengthened the brothers with many words."

questions.question: The council's letter said it "seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us" to lay no greater burden than the four requirements. This phrase affirmed what?
options: The Holy Spirit's active role in the council's decision-making
That the apostles had received a direct vision about this matter
That the decision had been voted on and unanimously passed
That the leaders had consulted the Scriptures and agreed together
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit's active role in the council's decision-making
questions.explanation: Acts 15:28 (ESV): "For it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay on you no greater burden than these requirements:"

key_verse_text: "But we believe that we will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will."
